wheel.lug_torque: 81 lb-ft (110 N·m) per Limitless Tire [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]

max_tire.note: Owners run 235/85R16 and 255/85R16 with no rubbing on stock suspension, and an '05 runs LT265/70R17. A 285/75R16 rubs at full lock and comes close to the inner fender.
An owner with a 2 in OME lift runs 255/85R16s with no issues. With IRS the lift doesn't change the wheel's swing, so 285/75R16 still rubs at full lock on OME medium springs.
One owner runs 34x10.5R17 on 17x7 wheels with 4.90 gears after trimming and massaging the front liners; it touches only on big impacts. Others warn a 34 is gutless without regearing.

items.title: Hydraulic brake booster accumulator can leak
items.summary: An improperly made accumulator can lose its nitrogen charge, causing a noise from the dash and delayed brake assist after the truck has been parked. Dealers fitted an improved accumulator. Australia's REC-003136 covers 13,488 NM/NP Pajeros for the same part.

items.title: Fuel tank leveling valve may leak
items.summary: With a full tank, parked nose-up on a slope, expanding fuel can get past the leveling valve and leak onto the ground. Dealers replace the valve.

items.title: Tire and loading label capacity weights wrong
items.summary: The label's capacity figures were wrong and could lead owners to exceed GVWR; replacement labels were mailed.

items.title: Bilingual airbag warning labels too small
items.summary: Removable English/Spanish airbag labels on the dash and visor didn't meet FMVSS 208 size rules.

items.title: Owner's manual missing tether-strap headrest instructions
items.summary: The manual didn't explain headrest adjustment when fitting a child-seat tether, as FMVSS 225 requires.

items.title: Passenger-side exterior mirror non-compliant
items.summary: Some passenger mirrors didn't meet FMVSS 111; dealers replace the mirror.

tsbs.title: Hydraulic brake booster: spilled fluid can damage the pump motor
tsbs.ref: Mitsubishi HBB notice (reported by JDMBUYSELL; six chassis codes)
tsbs.summary: Spilled brake fluid entering the pump motor caused malfunction and weak assist. Wipe up spills, never wash them away with water, and have a warning lamp, buzzer or poor braking checked with Mitsubishi's tester.

timeline.change: Third generation goes on sale in Japan (Mitsubishi gives 2 September; Wikipedia gives 2 August for its introduction). Monocoque with built-in frame, four-wheel independent suspension, Super Select 4WD II, 3.5 GDI V6 and 3.2 DI-D diesel
Australian NM launched with the 3.5 V6 and carry-over 2.8 4M40 diesel. Mitsubishi enters a T2 rally car based on the new Pajero at the Dakar

First US model year: Montero XLS and Limited, LWB only, 3.5 V6 (200 hp). Consumer Reports rates the Limited 'Not Acceptable' in June. US recall 01V254001 for the brake-booster accumulator (2001–02). Kleinschmidt wins the Dakar
Australia: the 3.2 DI-D replaces the 2.8 diesel and can be had with the five-speed auto. Owners recommend the diesel over the petrols and praise its durability
US recall 04V319000: fuel-tank leveling valve can leak when parked nose-up with a full tank
Facelift. US Montero gets the 3.8 6G75 V6 (215 hp per BaT) and M-ASTC; 20th Anniversary Edition. Owners say the XLS was dropped after this year
Electronic traction control added in Australia. ANCAP tests the Pajero Exceed
Japan: the 3.8 V6 (219 PS) arrives in the Super Exceed in November, replacing the GDI V6
Final US model year for the Montero. The fourth-generation Pajero launches in Japan on 4 October

identify.intro: US Monteros are straightforward, but imported Pajeros come in many codes and engines, and the 1999 cut-over means some '99 Pajeros are second-generation trucks.

items.head: Chassis codes
items.body: JDMBUYSELL lists V63W, V65W, V68W, V73W, V75W and V78W. Bring a Trailer's imports include a V65W three-door 3.5, a V68W three-door 3.2 diesel and a V75W five-door 3.5. Confirm the full code on the frame or VIN plate.

items.head: Second or third generation?
items.body: A 1999 Pajero can be either. Third-generation codes start V6 or V7; BaT's 1999 'Wide Exceed' with a V45 code is a second-generation truck with a separate frame.

items.head: US engine from the VIN
items.body: On BaT's US trucks, the 3.5 Monteros carry R as the eighth VIN character (JA4MW51R…) and the 3.8s carry S (JA4MW51S…, JA4NW31S…).

items.head: Pre-facelift or facelift
items.body: Mitsubishi facelifted the truck for 2003; in the US that's also when the 3.8 and M-ASTC arrived. BaT's 2003 and 2004 Limiteds list M-ASTC.

items.head: Grey-import tells
items.body: Right-hand drive, a fender-mounted mirror and a km/h speedometer (BaT's 1999 V68W has a 180 km/h speedo) mark a Japanese-market truck. Ask for the import paperwork.

values.intro: Third-generation Monteros are still cheap; clean, low-mileage Limiteds are the only ones that break $15,000, and Japanese diesels are just starting to arrive.
values.note: Based on 24 third-generation Montero and Pajero sales on Bring a Trailer from February 2022 to August 2026, from $3,750 (a 2001 Limited) to $19,777 (a 54k-mile 2001 Limited), median about $12,500. A 225k-mile 2003 20th Anniversary Edition brought $5,200 and a 1999 V68W 3.2 diesel import $14,600. JDMBUYSELL's seller-reported median for imports is $12,183 (n=6).

paragraphs: Only the long-wheelbase V6 Montero was sold new in the US. Short-wheelbase three-doors, the 3.0 V6, the 3.5 GDI and the 3.2 DI-D diesel are gray-market trucks. NHTSA's exemption covers vehicles at least 25 years old by their own manufacture date (49 CFR 591.5(i)), so as of October 2026 trucks built up to about October 2001 qualify and the rest follow month by month until the last ones in 2031. Bring a Trailer has already sold a 1999 V68W 3.2 diesel and a 2000 V65W three-door with import documents.

The EPA exemption is separate: JDMBUYSELL notes it requires at least 21 years and the original configuration, or an equivalent or newer EPA-certified engine and emissions system. State titling and emissions rules vary, and California is the hardest. Canada's 15-year threshold doesn't make a truck legal to bring into the US.
